thread:
Alex: Quick sync — ops ticket to change admission control in eu-west for GPU pools. Thinking of moving from hard reject to a sampled soft-queue + degrade mode for best-effort requests. want opinions.
Jordan: Can you sketch the flow? hard rejects are cheap but noisy. soft-queue might amplify tail latency if we aren't careful.
Alex: Yeah. Proposal: keep reserved-slot fastpath for paid SLAs, but for standard tier, sample x% of requests into a soft-queue that executes on a slowpath (lower batch priority, quantized model) rather than rejecting. If queue > threshold we still reject.
Maria: I like sampled approach for smoothing bursts. How do we pick x and thresholds? also need to ensure KV cache semantics aren't broken for chat sessions.
Alex: Initial plan: x=15% for peak windows, threshold queue depth 2000 tokens, degrade to quantized-8bit model and reduced context window (drop >512 prefix). Canonical fallback chain: fastpath -> soft-queue slowpath -> reject.
Sam: Cost question: slowpath still consumes GPU cycles; if we scale slowpath too much we pay more than before. Need a cost cap per-minute per-region.
Jordan: Agreed. Maybe cap slowpath concurrency to a fixed fraction of pool (e.g., 10% of GPUs) and route sampled traffic there. If cap reached, fall back to reject.
Maria: Also flagging network concerns: last week we saw intra-region networking spikes that delayed KV warmups. Soft-queue might increase cold-KV pressure. Suggest we only enable for models with small KV sizes.
Alex: Good point. We'll gate by model profile: allow soft-queue for models where avg KV < 64MB and token latency on slowpath < 600ms.
InfraAlertBot: [alert] eu-west-gpu-pool saturation spike detected 2025-11-24T08:10:23Z — 78% queue growth in 5m
Alex: that alert was during the spike we want to mitigate. We simulated earlier and saw 25% fewer hard rejects but 40% more slowpath invocations.
Sam: Simulation results ok, but what's user-visible quality? did you run our evals?
Alex: Ran the reconciler eval set: degrade mode increased hallucination signal in 3% of tests for long-context prompts. We can mitigate by only using degrade for stateless generation and not for chat/completions that rely on long context.
Jordan: Ops rollout plan? I'd prefer a canary: enable sampled soft-queue in a single AZ (eu-west-1a) at 1% traffic, monitor latency, errors, hallucination metric, and cost-per-token.
Maria: We'll need a dashboard: per-route slowpath rate, slowpath concurrency, per-GPU slowpath share, and the KV cold-hit rate. Also add a regression alert if hallucination delta > 1.5% in 5m.
Alex: Agreed. I'll draft a policy config. Preview:
Maria: paste the config so infra can review.
Alex: ```yaml
admission_policy:
  name: sampled-degrade-v1
  regions: [eu-west]
  gates:
    - name: sla_fastpath
      allow: tier == "enterprise"
    - name: sampled_softqueue
      allow: tier != "enterprise"
      sample_pct: 15
      max_slowpath_gpu_fraction: 10
      model_filters:
        - max_kv_mb: 64
        - excluded_types: ["chat_session"]
      slowpath_profile:
        quantization: q8_0
        max_context_tokens: 512
  hard_reject_if: queue_tokens > 2000
  metrics:
    emit: [slowpath_rate, slowpath_concurrency, hallucination_delta]
```
Jordan: config looks reasonable. One nit: sample_pct should be dynamic based on RPS. Better to express as min(max(0.15, load_based_pct), 0.5) or similar.
Sam: Also add a budget clamp: if slowpath_cost/minute > $X then reduce sample_pct to 0.
Maria: Ops detail: deploy needs a rollout job that can flip sample_pct via feature flag; plus a circuit breaker that auto-rejects when slowpath queue growth > 30% in 2m.
Alex: We'll add feature flag and circuit breaker. Plan: PR config -> infra canary in eu-west-1a @1% -> expand to 10% after 2h stable -> expand to full region if metrics stable for 24h.
InfraAlertBot: [deploy] admission-policy/sampled-degrade-v1 scheduled for canary: 2025-11-24T14:00:00Z by Alex
Jordan: Ping me when canary starts, I'll watch latency and errors.
Sam: I'll add cost cap and automatic scale-down hook.
Maria: I'll prepare dashboards and a short runbook for oncall: steps to disable sampled-degrade if hallucination spike or cost runaway.
Alex: Thanks team. I'll open the PR with config and test results. :thumbsup:
Jordan: :100:
Sam: 👍
